The steering committee met on Tuesday to review the quarterly results of the European subsidiaries. Revenue grew by four percent compared with the same period last year, mainly thanks to the new pricing model introduced in the spring. Operating costs, however, rose faster than expected because of higher energy prices and a delayed migration of the billing platform. The finance team proposed three measures: renegotiating the two largest supplier contracts, postponing non-essential hiring until the end of the year, and accelerating the decommissioning of the legacy data centre. Members asked for a detailed timeline and a risk assessment for each measure before the next meeting. The chair reminded everyone that the board expects a consolidated forecast by the fifteenth of next month, including a sensitivity analysis on exchange rates and interest rates. Several members noted that the customer satisfaction survey showed a slight decline in the retail segment, which they attributed to longer response times at the call centre. A working group will investigate staffing levels and the quality of the knowledge base used by agents. Finally, the committee approved the budget for the pilot project on automated invoice processing, which should reduce manual work by about a third if the results are confirmed.
